_readme: DATED SNAPSHOTS OF A1'S INTEREST RATE PROJECTIONS PAGE. Append-only.
Their page has a currency filter and nothing else -- no date control, no
history, no revision log -- so a projection read today cannot be rewound to a
past board. The only way this series ever becomes replayable is by reading it
again on a new day and appending. That is why this file exists separately from
the round fixtures: those record what was true on one day, this accumulates.
ONE ENTRY PER READING. Never edit an existing entry to 'correct' it -- a
reading is a fact about a day, and a page that has since changed does not make
yesterday's reading wrong. Append a new one.
`observedAt` is OUR reading date and is the only date used for replay.
AS OF 2026-09-01 THIS IS A PRODUCTION INPUT. The 2026-09-01 reading is the first that
covers all eight majors, which is what unblocked the rule -- a differenced column cannot
be adopted one currency at a time. `resolveConsensusProjectionLegs` is all-or-nothing for
exactly that reason: a board where any major is uncovered uses none of this.
`quarterValueStep` records how coarsely a reading was transcribed, and the resolver treats
anything within half a step of the standing rate as unreadable rather than as a move.

snapshots.source: a1trading.com EdgeFinder -> Interest Rate Projections, and Interest Rates - Historical Data (both free)
snapshots.provenance: Transcribed from fixtures/a1-rates-and-index-2026-08-30.json, which recorded the same reading in its round context. Quarter values are tooltip-confirmed to one decimal; policy rates are the Interest Rates page's Aug 2026 bar, NOT the carry-trade scanner (the two disagree on EUR by 0.25 -- see that fixture's a1InternalRateInconsistency).

snapshots.source: a1trading.com/interest-rates-data/ -> the embedded EdgeFinder "Free Economic Data" Looker report, page "Interest Rate Projections"; standing rates from fixtures/a1-policy-rates-2026-08-31.csv (their Interest Rates page, read 2026-08-31).
snapshots.provenance: Read from the bar chart's own hover tooltips, which print every selected currency for one quarter at once. Taken in two passes because the currency filter caps what is legible: AUD/CAD/CHF/NZD first, then AUD/CAD/CHF/EUR/GBP/JPY/USD, with AUD, CAD and CHF read in BOTH passes and identical in both -- that overlap is the only check available that the filter change did not move the series. THE TOOLTIP ROUNDS TO ONE DECIMAL, hence quarterValueStep 0.1: AUD 4.4 against a standing 4.35 and CAD 2.3 against 2.25 are each exactly half a step away and CANNOT be told from equality, which is why the resolver refuses to call them. A 25bp move would round clear of the band, so the rounding cannot hide a real decision.
